title: Private control plane: transient session storm after orchestrator upgrade — debrief & remediation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a staged orchestrator upgrade in a subset of customer Private/VPC clusters (canary cohort), we observed a coordinated burst of agent reconnections that caused transient control plane API saturation and NAT gateway ephemeral port exhaustion in some VPC setups. Symptoms included: agents repeatedly opening/closing sessions, prolonged control plane API 429/503 responses, increased request latencies for control plane operations, and in a small number of clusters, failed deployments due to lost websocket sessions. Impact window: ~2026-02-10T03:12Z to 2026-02-10T03:47Z. Root cause (summary): a change in the orchestrator's health/leader renewal behaviour (leader handoff sequence shortened) combined with an accidental removal of jitter from agents' reconnect logic in the same release resulted in synchronized reconnect attempts. The synchronized reconnects exceeded API rate limits and forced high TCP connection churn behind customer NAT gateways, leading to ephemeral port depletion and further session failures. This exposed gaps in our upgrade gating for private deployments and insufficient enforcements for randomized reconnect backoff and pre-upgrade capacity checks.
timeline_highlights: 2026-02-10 03:08Z: Rolling upgrade started for orchestrator v2026.02.1 (canary cohort).
2026-02-10 03:12Z: Alert fired: controlplane API 5xx rate increased for cluster-group A.
2026-02-10 03:18Z: Observed spike in agent websocket reconnects correlated with orchestrator pod restarts.
2026-02-10 03:25Z: Multiple clusters reported elevated application errors as controlplane operations were rate-limited.
2026-02-10 03:40Z: Mitigation: pause upgrade rollout and enable emergency reconnect-jitter rollout to canary cohort.
2026-02-10 03:47Z: Control plane latencies began to return to baseline as reconnects staggered and API rate-limits subsided.
root_cause_analysis: Code regression: reconnect backoff jitter was accidentally removed in commit fa3b9c (agent reconnect library).
Orchestrator behaviour: leader transition window reduced which caused batches of agents to interpret transient controller unavailability as final and immediately reconnect.
Operational: rollout gating did not simulate real NAT-limited customer network conditions — canary cohort selection missed environments with aggressive SNAT/NAT rules.
Reliability gap: control plane API rate limiter allowed short high-amplitude bursts with insufficient per-agent smoothing or burst token bucket limits per-project.
Networking: some customer NAT gateways had low ephemeral port ranges by default and no prior instrumentation for ephemeral port utilization in our agent diagnostics.
mitigations_deployed: Immediate: paused orchestrator rollout at canary and reverted agent reconnect behavior for affected cohorts (hotfix release agent-1.23.2).
Temporary: enabled an emergency server-side reconnect-jitter gate forcing randomized reconnection windows for agents from 30-3000ms.
Monitoring: added temporary alert for ephemeral port exhaustion indicators derived from increased short-lived TCP connections observed in metrics.

ENG-273942: Implement staggered upgrade preflight that queries representative client NAT behavior and simulates reconnect storms before canary promotion — owner: Lina Chen — due: 2026-03-05
ENG-273943: Add per-agent and per-project smoothing to control plane API rate limiter; implement burst caps — owner: Omar Haddad — due: 2026-03-12
ENG-273944: Add ephemeral port utilization telemetry in agent diagnostics and dashboards (instrumentation + customer-visible metric) — owner: Priya Nair — due: 2026-03-10

runbook_updates: Add a step to verify agent reconnect jitter is enabled in new releases and add a pre-rollout automated check.
Document NAT-capacity validation steps: how to detect short ephemeral port ranges and recommended remediation for customers.
Add guidance to abort/rollback rollout when control plane 5xx rate > 1.5x baseline for more than 5 minutes during canary.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Increasing jitter too aggressively may prolong some reconnection times for legitimately disconnected agents; we balance this against avoiding systemic storms.
Adding per-agent rate caps reduces peak API throughput per customer; need to validate tail latencies for high-throughput tenants.
Preflight NAT simulation increases release duration; mitigated by automating and running in parallel with existing checks.
